newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. to ask China to end poultry import curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to ask China to end poultry import curbs.

text.p: The United States Friday denied Chinese accusations of an outbreak of a disease in poultry in Oklahoma and Missouri and said it sought talks with China to lift a ban on poultry imports from them.

"Newcastle disease broke out in pet birds only ... All of the pet birds that were infected with the disease have been destroyed," a spokeswoman for the U.S. embassy in Beijing said. She said she had no information on which states found pet birds with Newcastle disease or when the problems were discovered.
The United States was seeking to hold talks with Chinese quarantine officials to try to convince them to lift a ban on poultry from the two states that was announced on Tuesday, the spokeswoman said.
The official Xinhua news agency said five cases of the disease were discovered in Oklahoma and Missouri between July and September.

An official of China's State Bureau of Animal Plant and Quarantine said the bureau was aware of the U.S. argument that the disease was found only in pet birds. But the official said the United States had not formally requested talks with the bureau.

In October, China announced a ban on imports of poultry from 10 U.S. states because of fears it carried a virus called highly pathogenic avian influenza. China and the United States held talks on the issue and the ban did not go into effect.
China is the second-biggest market in the world, after Russia, for U.S. poultry products.
Beijing and Washington are also at odds over textile imports, and that dispute has threatened to spill over into the farm sector.
China had threatened to ban effective last Tuesday some U.S. farm goods -- as well as textiles and alcoholic drinks -- in retaliation for U.S. penalties on textiles purchased from China.
However, Beijing announced this week that it was delaying implementing those curbs for one month because the two sides were planning further talks on the issue.
